newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber finishes steady in holiday market.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber finishes steady in holiday market.

text.p: Rubber futures closed slightly firmer on Thursday in very slow trade with players hoping the spot expiry in Japan may perk up the market tomorrow ahead of the Christmas holiday period, dealers said.

"The volumes today were terrible. This is already a pre-holiday market. We'll just see if the spot expiry in Japan can provide a spark for the market tomorrow," a dealer for a Western rubber trading company said.
"It's dead today. People were beginning to leave for the holidays, especially since Japan is closed on Monday," one trader said, refering to Emperor Akihito's birthday in Japan.
The only trades done were for 250 tonnes of RSS3 rubber and 75 tonnes of RSS1 rubber. There were no trades for TSR20 rubber.
"It was a very flat day. Everybody fell asleep," one trader said. "The volumes were pathetic."
At around 0945 GMT, January RSS3 was seen at 124.50-125.50 U.S. cents a kg compared with the previous 124.50 cents.
April/June RSS1 was seen at 185.50-186.50 Singapore cents (US$1.32-$1.33) a kg against 185.25 cents.
February TSR20 was indicated at 171.00-173.00 Singapore cents (US$1.22-$1.23) a kg from 172.75 cents.
